scope.recorded_clock: Queue wait plus modeled uplink; excludes local compute and global-model downlink. Completion means five prescribed FU steps, not certified deletion.
scope.fixed_order_accounting: Diagnostic only: preserve logged arrival/transaction order; add per-transaction maximum device compute time and complete model broadcast time to each request interval. Includes final broadcast to all UAVs. No overlap is assumed. Does not recompute periodic triggers, request arrivals, channel designs or model updates.
scope.downlink: Existing model: (20480*32+512) bits / 1 Mbps = 0.655872 seconds per nonzero uplink transaction.
scope.arrivals: Triggered by FL progress, not common external timestamps. Nine bursts of five requests, one seed. Requests in the same burst are correlated.
scope.throughput: All methods completed the same 45 requests. Requests per occupied uplink second measures realized radio-work efficiency, not maximum sustainable load or end-to-end throughput.
scope.deadline: Not evaluated: current deadline_s is null. Historical old_* deadlines are not active and are not reused.
scope.quality: KL<=0.01 is an existing reference-similarity diagnostic, not a privacy/deletion certificate. Fast five-step completion is distinct from matching a quality threshold.
scope.controls: Proposed/S-OF+ use the same CLIPErase-inspired objective; S-AC/AC-OF use the proxy objective. S-OF+ permits the previously authorized network-energy overruns.
scope.inference: A real-time scheduler with compute/downlink, fixed external arrivals and a load sweep is needed to establish end-to-end latency, capacity and deadline compliance.

assumptions: RF energy is the recorded conservative waveform bound divided by PA efficiency.
Nine scheduled transmit circuits and one receive circuit are active during uplink; no coefficient-aware circuit sleep.
Each nonzero transaction broadcasts the 32-bit aggregate and one 512-bit control message at 1 Mbps to nine peers.
Compute uses a CMOS cycle model with fixed explicit scenario constants, not an RTX3080 timing-to-UAV conversion.
The two adapter matrix products cost 10240 MACs per modality sample; gradient calls have factor3, accounting for forward and two backward products.

Frozen-encoder MAC model includes transformer attention/projections/MLPs and patch/projection layers; activation, normalization, memory, and system overhead are represented only by the active-board overhead term.
Cold feature construction and initial/proxy20 occur before takeoff and are charged once per independently deployed arm.
At each site, UAV computations occur in parallel; sum of the per-update maximum device time forms the synchronous compute critical path.
Site hover is max(prescribed60s, compute+uplink+broadcast+logged_wait). Travel retains actual formation displacements and original segment durations.
All vehicles complete the same full return route; extra workload extends hovering. Vertical takeoff/landing and acceleration transients are outside the fixed-altitude scenario.
